zebralogic.title: Consolidate Direct Equivalences
zebralogic.principle: When a clue directly equates two attribute values (e.g., "Arnold loves baseball"), treat them as a single linked entity and propagate all other constraints attached to either side of the equivalence.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue states that two attribute values refer to the same person, object, or house.
zebralogic.example: Model treats "Arnold loves baseball" and "Arnold loves romance books" as unrelated facts, ending up assigning Arnold to two different houses.

zebralogic.title: Assign Fixed Positions Immediately
zebralogic.principle: If a clue pins an attribute to a specific house number, place that attribute at the indicated house right away and immediately propagate any other attributes linked to that house.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue contains an absolute position such as "House 4's sport is basketball" or "the boba tea drinker is in the fourth house".
zebralogic.example: Model delays placing the known sport in house 4, later assigning a different sport to that house and creating a conflict.

zebralogic.title: Enforce Adjacency for 'next to' and Ordered Left
zebralogic.principle: Clues that use "next to", "directly left of", or "directly right of" require the two referenced houses to be adjacent (difference of exactly one). Enforce this adjacency separately from non‑adjacent ordering.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue contains the words "directly left of", "directly right of", "next to", or similar.
zebralogic.example: Model interprets "the country music lover is directly left of the hip‑hop lover" as a non‑adjacent ordering, placing them with a gap between.

zebralogic.title: Output Solution in Expected JSON Table Format
zebralogic.principle: The verifier expects a JSON object with a "header" array describing column order and a "rows" array of house entries; any deviation (missing keys, wrong order, extra text) leads to rejection.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: At the very end of the response, when presenting the final grid.
zebralogic.example: Model prints the grid as plain text lines without the required "header" and "rows" fields, causing the answer to be rejected.

zebralogic.title: Keep Reasoning Concise to Avoid Token Truncation
zebralogic.principle: Limit explanatory text before the final answer so the response stays within the model's token budget; otherwise the JSON may be cut off and become unparsable.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Throughout the response, especially before emitting the final JSON.
zebralogic.example: Model writes a long paragraph of step‑by‑step deductions, then the JSON answer is truncated and invalid.

zebralogic.title: Preserve Original Attribute Tokens (Case and Spelling)
zebralogic.principle: Copy attribute values exactly as they appear in the prompt, preserving capitalization, spacing, hyphens, and any special characters; mismatches cause the verifier to reject.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When writing attribute values into the final JSON.
zebralogic.example: Model outputs "hip‑hop" with a hyphen instead of the required "hip hop", leading to a mismatch.

zebralogic.title: Interpret Directional Ordering Correctly
zebralogic.principle: Distinguish between "somewhere to the left of" (non‑adjacent ordering) and "directly left of" (adjacent). Remember that house numbers increase from left to right, so "left of" means a lower number.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When processing any clue that mentions left/right or ordering.
zebralogic.example: Model swaps left and right, placing Alice to the right of the colonial house when the clue says she is left of it.

zebralogic.title: Enforce Exclusion Constraints for Specific House Numbers
zebralogic.principle: When a clue explicitly forbids an attribute from a particular house, treat that as a hard exclusion and never assign the attribute to that house during propagation.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue contains phrases like "cannot be in house 1" or "is not the person in the second house".
zebralogic.example: Model places Arnold in house 1 despite a clue stating he cannot be there.

zebralogic.title: Enforce Exact Distance Constraints
zebralogic.principle: When a clue specifies an exact number of houses between two attributes (e.g., "two houses between X and Y"), translate it into a precise numeric offset and enforce that offset during placement.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue mentions "between", "apart by", or gives a numeric distance.
zebralogic.example: Model treats "two houses between pop and classical" as "adjacent", ignoring the required one‑house gap.

zebralogic.title: Disambiguate Overlapping Attribute References
zebralogic.principle: If a word appears in multiple attribute categories, use context from the clue to decide which category it belongs to before applying the constraint.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When parsing clues that contain ambiguous terms that could belong to more than one attribute set.
zebralogic.example: Model interprets the word "modern" as a music genre when the clue actually refers to a house style.

zebralogic.description: Generating overly long reasoning before the final answer, causing token truncation.
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model tries to be exhaustive, producing many sentences of deduction, which consumes most of the token budget and leaves insufficient space for the complete JSON answer.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Keep the reasoning brief, summarize deductions, and reserve enough tokens for the final answer; optionally place the answer as the very last output.

zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model confuses the orientation of the house row or swaps the meaning of "left" and "right", leading to reversed placements.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Remember that house numbers increase from left to right; map "left of" to a lower house number and double‑check each directional clue.

zebralogic.description: Treating adjacency clues as non‑adjacent ordering, leading to placement errors.
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model reads "directly left of" as just "somewhere left of", ignoring the requirement that the houses be adjacent.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Enforce that adjacency clues require a difference of exactly one house; handle them separately from generic ordering clues.

zebralogic.description: Misinterpreting exact distance clues (e.g., "one house between") as adjacency or ignoring the distance.
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model either treats the distance as zero or discards the numeric offset, violating the precise spacing required.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Translate distance statements into a concrete offset (e.g., "one house between" → positions differ by 2) and enforce that offset during deduction.
